questions.question: The smallest natural number which is divisible by 33, 72, 11 and 18 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number must be divisible by 72, which means it must be a multiple of 9.

Using the divisibility rule of 9 (sum of digits must be divisible by 9) on the given options:

⇒ 881 → 8 + 8 + 1 = 17 | 839 → 8 + 3 + 9 = 20 | 696 → 6 + 9 + 6 = 21 (None are divisible by 9)

⇒ 792 → 7 + 9 + 2 = 18 (Divisible by 9)

Since only 792 is a multiple of 9, we can eliminate all other options instantly.

**∴ The correct answer is 792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 33, 72, 11, and 18.

**Method Used:**

The smallest natural number completely divisible by all given numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 33 = 3 × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 72 = 2³ × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 11 = 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ LCM = Highest powers of all prime factors present

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 3² × 11

⇒ LCM = 8 × 9 × 11

⇒ LCM = 72 × 11

⇒ LCM = 792

**∴ The correct answer is 792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is obtained by multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors present in the numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest positive integer that divides all the given numbers without leaving a remainder. It is the product of the lowest powers of common prime factors.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is perfectly divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.
</p

questions.question: Govind invested some money in HDFC at 3% per annum rate of interest. What would be the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) if after 2 years, Govind got ₹203 as compound interest, considering annual compounding?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of Compound Interest for 2 years = R + R + (R×R)÷100 = 3 + 3 + (3×3)÷100 = 6.09%.

Effective rate of Simple Interest for 2 years = 2 × R = 6%.

Given Compound Interest = 6.09% which is equal to ₹203.

Required Simple Interest = 6% ≡ (203 ÷ 6.09) × 6 = ₹200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Rate of interest (R) = 3% per annum

⇒ Time (T) = 2 years

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = ₹203

 
 Principal
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Year 1: 100u
 
 
 Year 2: 100u
 
 
• 
 3%

 
 Interest: 3u
 
 Total CI = 100u + 100u + 3u = 203u

**Method Used (Unit Assumption):**

⇒ Let the Simple Interest for 1 year be 100 units.

⇒ Simple Interest for the 2nd year = 100 units.

⇒ Compound interest on 1st year's interest at 3% = 3% of 100 = 3 units.

⇒ Total Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = 100 + 100 + 3 = 203 units.

⇒ Total Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = 100 + 100 = 200 units.

**Calculations:**

⇒ We are given CI = ₹203.

⇒ 203 units = ₹203

⇒ 1 unit = ₹1

⇒ Total SI = 200 units = 200 × 1 = ₹200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation for 2 Years

For a given rate R and time of 2 years, Compound Interest and Simple Interest are directly related by the formula: CI = SI × (1 + R ÷ 200).

Difference Between CI and SI (2 Years)

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is calculated as: D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Difference Between CI and SI (3 Years)

For 3 years, the standard difference formula is extended to: D = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100).

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years, the effective CI percentage can be quickly found using the successive percentage change formula: 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: P can complete a round of circular track in 1 minute and 30 seconds while Q can complete a round in 45 seconds. If they start moving from the same point and move in opposite directions, then they meet after _____ seconds.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two persons start simultaneously from the same point and move in opposite directions on a circular track, the time taken to meet is T = (T₁ × T₂) ÷ (T₁ + T₂).

⇒ T₁ = 90 seconds (1 min 30 sec), T₂ = 45 seconds

⇒ T = (90 × 45) ÷ (90 + 45)

⇒ T = 4050 ÷ 135 = 30 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 30 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P (T₁) = 1 minute 30 seconds = 90 seconds

Time taken by Q (T₂) = 45 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂

Time to meet = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 Start Point

 
 
 Meeting Point

 
 

 P (90 s)

 
 

 Q (45 s)
 
 
 Time to Meet = 30 seconds

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total length of the track be the LCM of 90 and 45 = 90 units.

⇒ Speed of P = 90 units ÷ 90 seconds = 1 unit/second.

⇒ Speed of Q = 90 units ÷ 45 seconds = 2 units/second.

⇒ Since they are moving in opposite directions, their relative speed is added up.

⇒ Relative Speed = Speed of P + Speed of Q = 1 + 2 = 3 units/second.

⇒ Time taken to meet = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 90 ÷ 3 = 30 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting in Same Direction

If two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is |S₁ − S₂|. The time taken to meet for the first time is T = (T₁ × T₂) ÷ |T₁ − T₂|.

Meeting at the Starting Point

Regardless of the direction of motion, the time taken for them to meet again exactly at the starting point is always the LCM of their individual times to complete one round.

Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a:b (in simplest form), the number of distinct meeting points on the track is (a + b) for opposite directions, and |a − b| for the same direction.
</p

questions.question: Six persons went to a hotel to have their meals. Five of them spent ₹30 each on their meals. The sixth person spent ₹50 more than the average expenditure of all the six. What was the total money spent by all the persons?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The 6th person pays the average amount plus an extra ₹50.

This extra ₹50 compensates for the remaining 5 persons who paid less than the average.

Deficit per person = 50 ÷ 5 = ₹10.

Average expenditure = 30 + 10 = ₹40.

Total expenditure of 6 persons = 6 × 40 = ₹240.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expenditure of 5 persons = ₹30 each

Expenditure of 6th person = Average expenditure of all 6 + ₹50

 
 
 

 
 

 
•

 Extra ₹50 balances the deficits (₹10 each)

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of Persons

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the average expenditure of all 6 persons be ₹x.

⇒ Total expenditure of 6 persons = 6x

⇒ Total expenditure = (Expenditure of 5 persons) + (Expenditure of 6th person)

⇒ 6x = (5 × 30) + (x + 50)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Average

The average of a given set of numbers is calculated as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations.

Deviation Method

The net deviation of all values from the average is always zero. If a value is greater than the average, it provides a positive deviation that perfectly balances the combined negative deviations of values strictly lesser than the average.

Combined Average

When combining two separate groups, the overall sum is simply the sum of the individual products of their respective averages and counts. Total Sum = (n₁ × A₁) + (n₂ × A₂).

questions.question: What is the highest number between 4000 and 5000, which when divided by 12, 16 and 24 would leave the remainder 4?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 12, 16, and 24 is 48.

The required number format is 48k + 4.

Divide the upper limit 5000 by 48 ⇒ Remainder = 8.

Highest multiple of 48 under 5000 = 5000 − 8 = 4992.

Required highest number = 4992 + 4 = 4996.

**∴ The correct answer is 4996.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 12, 16, and 24

Range = 4000 to 5000

Remainder = 4

**Concept Used:**

Number = LCM of divisors × k + Remainder

**Calculation:**

⇒ Prime factors of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factors of 16 = 2⁴

⇒ Prime factors of 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ LCM(12, 16, 24) = 2⁴ × 3 = 16 × 3 = 48

⇒ The required number must be of the form N = 48k + 4.

⇒ Divide 5000 by 48 to find the highest multiple under 5000.

⇒ 5000 ÷ 48 = 104 with a remainder of 8.

⇒ Highest multiple of 48 under 5000 = 5000 − 8 = 4992.

⇒ Substitute the multiple back to find the number:

⇒ N = 4992 + 4 = 4996.

⇒ 4996 clearly lies within the target range of 4000 to 5000.

**∴ The correct answer is 4996.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM with Constant Remainder

When finding a number that leaves the same remainder r when divided by a, b, and c, use the form: N = LCM(a, b, c) × k + r.

LCM with Different Remainders

If a number divided by a, b, and c leaves remainders x, y, and z respectively, and the difference is constant (a−x = b−y = c−z = K), the number format is: N = LCM(a, b, c) × k − K.

HCF with Given Remainders

The greatest number that divides a, b, and c leaving remainders x, y, and z respectively is given by HCF of (a−x), (b−y), and (c−z).
</p

questions.question: There are 81 members in group A, 29 members in group B and 70 members in group C. All the members of these groups went to a restaurant. The average amount spent on each member of group A, B and C is ₹467, ₹117 and ₹378, respectively. The total average amount (in ₹) spent per member is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can use the Deviation Method by assuming an average close to the given values, say ₹378.

Deviations from ₹378: Group A = +89, Group B = −261, Group C = 0.

Total deviation = (81 × 89) + (29 × −261) + (70 × 0) = 7209 − 7569 = −360.

Actual combined average = Assumed Average + (Total deviation ÷ Total members) = 378 + (−360 ÷ 180) = 378 − 2 = ₹376.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹376.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 Group A (81)
 ₹467
 
 
 
 Group B (29)
 ₹117

 
 
 Group C (70)
 ₹378

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Total Members = 81 + 29 + 70 = 180
 Overall Average = ₹376

**Given:**

Number of members in Group A = 81, Average amount spent = ₹467

Number of members in Group B = 29, Average amount spent = ₹117

Number of members in Group C = 70, Average amount spent = ₹378

**Formula Used:**

Total Average = (Total amount spent by all groups) ÷ (Total number of members)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total members = 81 + 29 + 70 = 180

⇒ Total amount spent by Group A = 81 × 467 = ₹37827

⇒ Total amount spent by Group B = 29 × 117 = ₹3393

⇒ Total amount spent by Group C = 70 × 378 = ₹26460

⇒ Total amount spent by all members = 37827 + 3393 + 26460 = ₹67680

⇒ Total average amount per member = 67680 ÷ 180 = ₹376

**∴ The correct answer is ₹376.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When combining groups of different sizes, the combined average is a weighted average. Formula: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂ + n₃A₃) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + n₃).

Deviation Method

To quickly find the average of large numbers, pick an assumed average (A). The true average = A + (Sum of all deviations ÷ Total number of observations). This is extremely helpful in eliminating calculation-heavy multiplication.

Properties of Average

If every observation in a set is increased or decreased by a constant value 'k', the new average also increases or decreases by exactly 'k'.

questions.question: If the curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of height 12 cm is 96 π cm², then its radius is:
questions.solution:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = 2πrh

⇒ 2 × π × r × 12 = 96π

⇒ 24π × r = 96π

⇒ r = 4 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 CSA = 96π cm²

**Given:**

Height of the cylinder (h) = 12 cm

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 96π cm²

**Formula Used:**

CSA of a right circular cylinder = 2πrh

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2 × π × r × 12 = 96π

⇒ 24π × r = 96π

⇒ r = 96π ÷ 24π

⇒ r = 4 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area encompasses both the curved face and the two flat circular bases. Formula: TSA = 2πr(r + h)

Volume of a Cylinder

The amount of 3D space occupied by a right circular cylinder. Formula: Volume = πr²h

Curved Surface Area of a Cone

For a right circular cone having base radius r and slant height l. Formula: CSA = πrl

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹1,500, a man gains ₹150. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to gain 24%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price = Selling Price − Gain

CP = 1500 − 150 = ₹1,350

New Selling Price to gain 24% = 124% of Cost Price

New SP = 1350 × 1.24 = ₹1,674

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,674.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹1,500

Gain = ₹150

Target Gain = 24%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain

Selling Price (New) = CP × [(100 + Gain%) ÷ 100]

 
 
 CP
 ₹1350

 ₹1500
 
 
 
 SP2
 ₹1674

 
 

 

 Gain = ₹150

 

 

 Gain = 24%

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = 1500 − 150 = ₹1,350

⇒ Target Gain = 24% of 1350

⇒ Target Gain = (24 ÷ 100) × 1350

⇒ Target Gain = 24 × 13.5 = ₹324

⇒ New Selling Price = CP + Target Gain

⇒ New SP = 1350 + 324 = ₹1,674

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,674.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the equivalent single discount is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂ ÷ 100)]%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells at cost price but uses a false weight, the actual Profit % is calculated by [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100%.

Marked Price & Profit Relationship

Discount is always applied on the Marked Price (MP). To find the relation between CP and MP when Profit is P% and Discount is D%: CP × (100 + P)% = MP × (100 − D)%.

questions.question: Manoj travels from City A to City B. If Manoj drives his car at (3)/(5) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 10 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Manoj would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time.

Ratio of Normal Speed to New Speed = 5 : 3

Ratio of Normal Time to New Time = 3 : 5

Difference in time ratio = 5 − 3 = 2 units.

Given delay = 10 minutes ⇒ 2 units = 10 mins ⇒ 1 unit = 5 mins.

Normal time = 3 units = 3 × 5 = 15 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = 3/5 × Normal speed

Delay in reaching City B = 10 minutes

 
• 
 
 
 
 City A
 City B
 
 Distance = Constant
 
 
 Normal Speed = S
 Normal Time = T
 
 
 New Speed = 3/5 S
 New Time = T + 10

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the normal speed be S and the normal time taken be T minutes.

⇒ Since the distance travelled is constant in both cases:

⇒ Distance at normal speed = Distance at new speed

⇒ S × T = (3/5 × S) × (T + 10)

⇒ T = 3/5 × (T + 10)

⇒ 5 × T = 3 × (T + 10)

⇒ 5T = 3T + 30

⇒ 5T − 3T = 30

⇒ 2T = 30

⇒ T = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality

When distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional. If speed changes to a/b of the original, time changes to b/a of the original.

Average Speed

If two equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the whole journey is (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. For opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
</p

questions.question: The fourth proportional to 5, 35 and x is 84, find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the multiplier relationship between the first and second term is identical to the third and fourth term.

Ratio of the first two terms is 5 : 35, which means the second term is 7 times the first.

Therefore, the fourth term must also be 7 times the third term (x).

x × 7 = 84 ⇒ x = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 5, 35, x and the fourth proportional is 84.

**Formula Used:**

For any four numbers in proportion, a : b :: c : d ⇒ a ÷ b = c ÷ d.

 
 
 

 
 
 
 a = 5
 
 b = 35
 

 × 7
 ::
 
 c = x
 
 d = 84
 

 × 7

**Calculation:**

⇒ 5 ÷ 35 = x ÷ 84

⇒ 1 ÷ 7 = x ÷ 84

⇒ x = 84 ÷ 7

⇒ x = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is calculated as √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If c is the third proportional to a and b, then a : b :: b : c, which implies c = b² ÷ a.

Continued Proportion

Three non-zero numbers a, b, c are said to be in continued proportion if the ratio of the first to the second is equal to the ratio of the second to the third (a : b = b : c).
</p

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 25 days and 30 days, respectively. They worked together for 6 days, after while B was replaced by P and the work was finished in the next 8 days. How long will P alone take to complete the same work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(25, 30) = 150 units. Efficiency of A = 6, B = 5.

Work completed by A and B in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units. Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.

Work done by A in the next 8 days = 6 × 8 = 48 units. So, work done by P in 8 days = 84 − 48 = 36 units.

Efficiency of P = 36 ÷ 8 = 4.5 units/day. Time taken by P alone = 150 ÷ 4.5 = 33 ¹/₃ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 33 ¹/₃ days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 25 days

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 30 days

⇒ They worked together for = 6 days

⇒ Time A and P worked together for remaining work = 8 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total work be the LCM of 25 and 30.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 25
 150
 150 ÷ 25 = 6
 
 

 B
 30
 150 ÷ 30 = 5
 
 

⇒ Work done by A and B in 6 days = (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B) × 6

⇒ Work completed in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 11 × 6 = 66 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work completed

⇒ Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units

⇒ For the remaining work, A and P worked together for 8 days.

⇒ Work done by A in these 8 days = 6 × 8 = 48 units

⇒ Work done by P in 8 days = Total remaining work − Work done by A

⇒ Work done by P = 84 − 48 = 36 units

⇒ Efficiency of P = Work done ÷ Time taken

⇒ Efficiency of P = 36 ÷ 8 = 4.5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by P alone to complete the total work = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of P

⇒ Time = 150 ÷ 4.5 = 1500 ÷ 45 = 100 ÷ 3 = 33 ¹/₃ days

**∴ The correct answer is 33 ¹/₃ days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to time and work problems, the total capacity of the tank is taken as the LCM of the individual filling or emptying times. Emptying pipes or leakages are treated as having negative efficiency.

Alternate Day Work

Instead of single days, calculate the total work done in a full cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers). Divide the total work by the cycle work to find the number of full cycles, then calculate the remaining work for the final fraction of days.

Work and Wages

Wages are directly distributed in proportion to the total amount of work done by each individual. If workers work together from start to finish, the wage ratio is identical to their efficiency ratio.
</p

questions.question: Raj has ₹1612 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Varun and Ashish and asked them to invest it at 8% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Varun and Ashish got same amount after 18 and 19 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Raj give to Varun?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal amounts, Ratio of Principals = (1 + R/100)Differeⁿce iⁿ Time

Ratio of Varun's share to Ashish's share = (1 + 8/100)¹⁹ − ¹⁸ = 108/100 = 27 : 25

Total parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts ≡ ₹1612

⇒ Varun's share = (27/52) × 1612 = 27 × 31 = ₹837

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum to be divided = ₹1612

Rate of Interest (R) = 8% p.a. compounded annually

Time for Varun (T₁) = 18 years

Time for Ashish (T₂) = 19 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest: A = P(1 + R/100)T

 
 Total: ₹1612
 

 

 

 
 
 Varun: T = 18 yrs
 Share: P1
 
 
 Ashish: T = 19 yrs
 Share: P2
 
 

 

 

 

 
 
 Equal Amount @ 8% CI p.a.
 Ratio P1 : P2 = 27 : 25

**Calculations:**

Let Varun's share be P₁ and Ashish's share be P₂.

⇒ P₁ + P₂ = 1612

According to the given condition, the amounts received by both are equal:

⇒ P₁(1 + 8/100)¹⁸ = P₂(1 + 8/100)¹⁹

Dividing both sides by (1 + 8/100)¹⁸:

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = (1 + 8/100)¹⁹ − ¹⁸

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = (1 + 8/100)¹

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = 108 / 100 = 27 / 25

The ratio of Varun's share to Ashish's share is 27 : 25.

⇒ Total ratio parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts

⇒ Value of 52 parts = ₹1612

⇒ Value of 1 part = 1612 ÷ 52 = ₹31

⇒ Varun's share (P₁) = 27 parts × 31 = ₹837

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compound Interest

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and time is doubled (2T). The formula becomes: A = P(1 + R/200)²T.

Difference Between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for exactly 2 years on a given principal is calculated using the formula: D = P(R/100)².

Rule of 72

A quick mental math rule used to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual fixed interest rate. Time to double ≈ 72 ÷ Rate of Interest.

questions.question: The LCM of 36, 45, 465 and 310 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Break the numbers into pairs to find the LCM efficiently.

LCM of 36 and 45 = 180

LCM of 465 and 310 = 31 × LCM(15, 10) = 31 × 30 = 930

Now find the LCM of the results: LCM of 180 and 930 = 30 × LCM(6, 31) = 30 × 186 = 5580

**∴ The correct answer is 5580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 36, 45, 465 and 310

**Formula Used:**

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved in the given numbers.

**Calculations:**

Step 1: Find the prime factorisation of each number.

⇒ 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ 45 = 3² × 5

⇒ 465 = 3 × 5 × 31

⇒ 310 = 2 × 5 × 31

Step 2: Extract the highest power of every prime factor present.

⇒ Highest power of 2 is 2²

⇒ Highest power of 3 is 3²

⇒ Highest power of 5 is 5¹

⇒ Highest power of 31 is 31¹

Step 3: Multiply them together to obtain the LCM.

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 × 31

⇒ LCM = 4 × 9 × 5 × 31

⇒ LCM = 36 × 155

⇒ LCM = 5580

**∴ The correct answer is 5580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Factorisation Method

To find the LCM, express each number as a product of prime numbers. The LCM is the product of the highest power of each prime factor present.

Relation Between HCF and LCM

For any two given numbers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM equals the product of the numbers: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

LCM of Fractions

To find the LCM of fractions, use the formula: LCM = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).
</p

questions.question: The price (per litre) of petrol increases by 50%. By what percent should its consumption be reduced such that the expenditure on it increases by 23% only?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial price and expenditure be 100.

New Price Base = 100 + 50 = 150

Desired Expenditure = 100 + 23 = 123

Percentage reduction in consumption = [(New Price − Desired Expenditure) ÷ New Price] × 100

⇒ [(150 − 123) ÷ 150] × 100 = (27 ÷ 150) × 100 = 18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 Initial = 100

 
 Exp = 123

 
 Price = 150

 

 +50% (Price Effect)

 

 Reduce by 27
 (150 − 123)

 

 +23% (Net Exp)

 Required % Reduction = (27 ÷ 150) × 100 = 18%

**Given:**

Increase in the price of petrol = 50%

Desired increase in expenditure = 23%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

**Calculations:**

Let the initial price of petrol be ₹100/litre and the initial consumption be 100 litres.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 100 = ₹10000

⇒ New Price = 100 + 50% of 100 = ₹150/litre

⇒ New Expenditure = 10000 + 23% of 10000 = ₹12300

⇒ New Consumption = New Expenditure ÷ New Price

⇒ New Consumption = 12300 ÷ 150 = 82 litres

⇒ Reduction in consumption = Initial Consumption − New Consumption = 100 − 82 = 18 litres

⇒ Required Percentage Reduction = (18 ÷ 100) × 100 = 18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

1. Price and Consumption Relationship

When expenditure is kept constant, Price and Consumption are inversely proportional. If price increases by R%, consumption must be reduced by (R ÷ (100 + R)) × 100%.

2. Successive Percentage Change

When a quantity experiences two consecutive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective net percentage change is given by the formula: Net % Change = a + b + (a × b ÷ 100).

3. Base Change Method

To calculate the required change from a new base value back to a desired value, use: % Change = (Difference ÷ New Base) × 100.

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers a festive offer: buy any three shirts, get two free. Find the equivalent percentage discount for the offer.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In Buy X Get Y Free offers, the discount percentage is calculated on the total number of items.

Total items = Paid items + Free items = 3 + 2 = 5

Discount % = (Free items ÷ Total items) × 100

Discount % = (2 ÷ 5) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of shirts paid for = 3

Number of shirts received free = 2

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Buy
 Buy
 Buy
 
 Free
 Free
 
 
 
• 
 Paid: 3 Shirts

 
• 
 Free: 2 Shirts
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total: 5 Shirts (Marked Price base)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the marked price of 1 shirt be ₹10.

⇒ Marked price of 5 shirts = 5 × 10 = ₹50

⇒ Since 2 shirts are given for free, the customer pays for only 3 shirts.

⇒ Selling price of the transaction = 3 × 10 = ₹30

⇒ Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price

⇒ Discount = 50 − 30 = ₹20

⇒ Discount % = (20 ÷ 50) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Marked Price (MP) is the price placed on the label. Discount is always calculated on the MP, while profit or loss is calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Buy X Get Y Free + Extra % Discount

In cases where an additional d% discount is given over a Buy X Get Y Free offer, first calculate the Selling Price after deducting the free items, then apply the extra d% discount on that value to find the final Selling Price.

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a weight that actually weighs 24% less than what is written on it. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a dishonest dealer selling at cost price, Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100

⇒ Error in weight = 24%

⇒ Profit % = [24 ÷ (100 − 24)] × 100

⇒ Profit % = (24 ÷ 76) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (6 ÷ 19) × 100 = 600 ÷ 19% = 31 ¹¹/₁₉%

**∴ The correct answer is 31 ¹¹/₁₉%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at Cost Price (CP).

He uses a false weight that is 24% less than the true weight.

 
 Billed Weight: 100 units (SP = ₹100)

 
 Actual Weight: 76 units (CP = ₹76)

 
 24% Less

 

 Profit = ₹24
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price of 100 units of weight be ₹100.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) for 100 units = ₹100 (as he promises to sell at CP).

⇒ The actual weight given to the customer = 100 − 24 = 76 units.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) for the actual 76 units given = ₹76.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 100 − 76 = ₹24.

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (24 ÷ 76) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (6 ÷ 19) × 100 = 600 ÷ 19

⇒ Profit % = 31 ¹¹/₁₉ %

**∴ The correct answer is 31 ¹¹/₁₉%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Selling at Markup

If a dealer marks up the goods by x% and also uses a false weight, calculate the overall profit using the ratio: CP / SP = (Actual Weight / Billed Weight) × [100 / (100 + x)].

Dishonest Dealer Selling at a Loss

If claiming to sell at a loss of L% but using false weight, actual profit or loss can be found by evaluating the net impact of the weight reduction against the loss percentage.

Successive Percentage Change

Net effect of two successive percentage changes a% and b% = (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%. This rule is widely applicable across profit and loss problems involving multiple stages.
</p
